title: Tone grilling, round 1
description: Step 1 of the Tone Development Plan: who reads the book, who you are to them, your moods, and 6 lines from epoch 6. 18 Nov 2026.
intro: Step 1 of the Tone Development Plan. Your notes are saved word for word into Book/build/tone/grilling.md.
No pick from Claude on any card. Write as much or as little as you like in the notes.

sections.title: The reader and you
sections.sub: Who you picture, and who you are to them.

cards.title: When you write a chapter, who is reading it?
options: a. A capable introvert who calls himself lazy and doesn't know why
b. One real client you picture while you write (name them in the note)
c. You, years ago, before coaching
d. Someone else (say who in the note)

cards.title: Who are you to that reader?
options: b. Fellow traveller, a few steps ahead
c. Editor who helps them reread their own story
e. Something else, or a mix (say which shows up when)

sections.title: Your moods
sections.sub: For each mood, how much it belongs in the book. In the note, say where: the opening story, the science part, the turn, or the ask at the end.

cards.title: Talking to yourself ("What do you mean?" I thought)
Amused by the crazy things people do
A mood of yours that is not on this list
cards.placeholder: Name it, and where it goes

sections.title: The David opening
sections.sub: The part before The Thrill of the First Day.

cards.title: When the reader finishes the David opening, what should they feel?
David's quotes: which fits what you want?
cards.context: Your comment on epoch 6 asked if the problem is how the quoted lines are written.
options: a. Fewer quotes: only the 2 or 3 lines that turn the story, and you tell the rest
b. Keep the quotes, but write them closer to how he really talked
c. Keep the quotes and the number, with more of your telling between them
d. Something else (say what in the note)

sections.title: Right or wrong tone
sections.sub: Six lines from epoch 6. A word on why helps, but is not needed.

cards.title: "Lazy people don't have weeks like that. Lazy people have empty weeks."
"So on the days fun won, a zero cost him nothing he had chosen, and of course he felt little about it."
"We live in a farmer's world with a gatherer's brain."
"Could have is a comfortable place to live. Nothing ever happens there, and nothing ever goes wrong."
"If you are a parent who has paid for your child's tutors, classes, or coaching, I don't think you did anything wrong."
"That is not the week of a lazy person. It is the week of someone with a full tank and nowhere chosen to drive."
